name: Japan Diabetes Society (JDS)
why_relevant: National diabetes research society, IDF member. Runs the EFSD-JDS Reciprocal Travel Research Fellowship with the European Foundation for the Study of Diabetes - a bilateral exchange programme for diabetes researchers between Europe and Japan
suggested_ask: Route through the EFSD-JDS fellowship framework: a German researcher presenting a human-baseline study is the profile the programme was built for. Ask about the annual scientific meeting as a presentation venue
dwih_angle: Direct fit: the DWIH Launchpad lands in Tokyo during JDS's active season; the EFSD reciprocal link gives the Rostock affiliation institutional weight
notes: JDS annual meeting is the largest diabetes venue in Japan. The EFSD fellowship is the single strongest institutional bridge found: European diabetes research explicitly paired with Japanese counterparts

name: Japan Association for Diabetes Education and Care (JADEC)
why_relevant: Patient-facing national body with 1600 local groups and 15000 members. Publishes monthly magazine Sakae (さかえ), the main Japanese diabetes patient publication
suggested_ask: Pitch an article in Sakae: a citizen-science study where anyone can play and compare their glucose prediction to a model. The magazine accepts patient experience contributions
dwih_angle: A German-Japanese research collaboration featured in a national patient magazine reaches the recruitment target through existing community infrastructure
notes: Sakae is the single best Japanese-language patient media found. JADEC also holds an annual scientific meeting and participates in IDF and AASD joint conferences

name: Japan IDDM Network (日本IDDMネットワーク)
why_relevant: Certified NPO for type 1 diabetes patients and families. Maintains a nationwide directory of local patient groups, funds research toward a cure
suggested_ask: Ask for a newsletter or website mention of the study, and introduction to their local group leaders who can share with adult members
dwih_angle: Type 1 community with national reach; the study recruits both T1D and non-diabetic adults
notes: Based in Saga Prefecture. Phone: 0952-20-2062 (weekdays 9-17). The network of local groups is the ground-level recruitment channel

name: National Center for Global Health and Medicine (NCGM)
why_relevant: One of six National Centers for Advanced and Specialized Medical Care. Runs diabetes and metabolic disease research. Hosts the Diabetes and Metabolism Information Center and the J-DREAMS database (Japan Diabetes compREhensive database project)
suggested_ask: Research collaboration: ask about the J-DREAMS database as a source of anonymised CGM traces, and about hosting a seminar on the human prediction baseline
dwih_angle: NCGM is in Tokyo and reachable through the DWIH network. The J-DREAMS project is the largest structured diabetes database in Japan
notes: Located in Shinjuku, Tokyo. The Bureau of International Health Cooperation handles overseas researcher contact. Tel: +81-3-3202-7181

name: Nagoya University - Niitsu Lab (新津葵一研究室)
why_relevant: Associate Professor Kiichi Niitsu's group in the Graduate School of Engineering developed an AI system that predicts blood glucose 30 minutes ahead using only CGM data and a specialised neural network, with live learning during operation
suggested_ask: Research contact: their 30-minute prediction system is the closest published Japanese work to Sugar-Sugar's prediction task. Propose a comparison or joint analysis - human prediction vs their model at overlapping horizons
dwih_angle: Direct overlap: both projects predict future glucose from CGM traces. A joint paper comparing human and model performance on the same data would serve both groups
notes: The system was published in 2019. Confirm current lab status and whether the group is still active on glucose prediction before contact. The lab is in the Faculty of Engineering, not the medical school

name: Chiba University Hospital - ICU Glucose Prediction Group
why_relevant: Developed machine learning models (XGBoost, random forest, neural networks) to predict hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia 6 hours ahead using electronic health records of 8853 ICU patients (2010-2022). Published in Scientific Reports, December 2025
suggested_ask: Research contact: their ICU glucose prediction is methodologically adjacent. Propose a cross-domain comparison or cite their work in the Sugar-Sugar protocol paper
dwih_angle: Demonstrates Japanese institutional expertise in ML-based glucose prediction, strengthening the case for Japanese collaboration
notes: The study is retrospective using EHR data, not CGM traces from ambulatory patients, so the prediction task is related but different. Worth a conversation, not a direct partnership

name: University of Electro-Communications / Juntendo University
why_relevant: Joint pilot study on predicting glucose metabolism disorder risk using XGBoost and SVM, with data from oral glucose tolerance tests (2006-2017). Faculty of Informatics and Engineering (UEC) + Department of General Medicine (Juntendo)
suggested_ask: Research contact: their ML approach to glucose risk prediction from clinical data complements Sugar-Sugar's CGM-trace approach. Offer a seminar or poster presentation at either institution
dwih_angle: Two Tokyo universities with established glucose prediction ML expertise - a natural audience for the human-baseline argument
notes: The pilot was published in 2018. Confirm current research direction before contact

name: Kyoto University - Dept. of Diabetes Endocrinology and Nutrition
why_relevant: Led by Professor Daisuke Yabe. Research covers islet biology, incretin secretion, genetic investigation of diabetes, obesity treatment, and clinical research. The department also works on personalised AI health plans with hierarchical Bayesian modelling
suggested_ask: Seminar or guest lecture during the DWIH Kansai leg: the Launchpad visits the Kansai region, and Kyoto University is the anchor research institution there
dwih_angle: Kansai leg of the DWIH Launchpad makes Kyoto a scheduled stop. A seminar at the diabetes department is a natural programme element
notes: Professor Yabe took up his post recently. Confirm interest in digital health and citizen science before proposing a full collaboration

name: Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine - Longevity and Community Epidemiology
why_relevant: Runs the Kyotango Longevity Cohort Study and co-organised the 1st World Longevity Summit with affiliates including University of Osaka and Altos Labs. Kyotango is one of Japan's famous longevity zones
suggested_ask: Research contact: the longevity angle - glucose regulation as a biomarker of healthy aging. Propose using Sugar-Sugar in a longevity cohort as a quick functional assessment
dwih_angle: The longevity connection is Anton's wider research context (enhancement.bio) and could open a second use case for the prediction task
notes: This is a stretch for direct Sugar-Sugar promotion but fits the DWIH partnership-building objective. Requires framing glucose prediction as a functional aging biomarker

name: Japan Agency for Medical Research and Development (AMED)
why_relevant: National funding agency for medical R&D. Runs AMED-CREST for advanced medical innovation and SICORP for strategic international collaborative research. Active joint calls with EU partners
suggested_ask: Explore upcoming SICORP or bilateral Germany-Japan calls. AMED's international collaboration department can advise on eligible mechanisms for a joint German-Japanese digital health study
dwih_angle: DWIH Tokyo lists AMED as a network partner. A funded collaboration is the highest-value outcome of the Launchpad trip
notes: AMED targets several European countries as collaborative partner countries. Check www.amed.go.jp/en/news/proposals.html for current open calls before the November trip

name: Japan Science and Technology Agency (JST)
why_relevant: National S&T funding body. Runs JSPS KAKENHI (already cited in glucose prediction research) and the J-STAGE open-access journal platform. Targets EU as collaborative partner
suggested_ask: Low-priority funding lead. Worth a meeting if the DWIH programme arranges institutional visits, but not a direct outreach target
dwih_angle: DWIH network partner
notes: JST's relevance is indirect: they fund the researchers, not the study directly. JSPS KAKENHI supported glucose prediction work at Kyushu University

name: National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST)
why_relevant: Japan's premier industrial research institution. Covers digital health, biosensors, and AI. DWIH network partner
suggested_ask: Meeting during the DWIH trip if scheduled. AIST's biosensor and digital health divisions are tangentially relevant
dwih_angle: DWIH network partner, likely on the Launchpad schedule
notes: Very broad institution. Identify the specific division (Health and Medical Research Institute or Information Technology and Human Factors division) before requesting a meeting

name: RIKEN - Center for Biosystems Dynamics Research
why_relevant: Japan's flagship research institution. The BDR centre studies life cycle from development through aging as continuous multilayered biological processes
suggested_ask: Low-priority research contact. Worth a conversation about aging biomarkers if the trip includes Kobe (BDR is in the Kobe campus)
dwih_angle: DWIH network partner. RIKEN BDR is in Kobe, between Tokyo and Kansai on the Launchpad route
notes: Very basic science, far from clinical. Only relevant if framing glucose prediction as a systems-biology aging phenotype

name: ARKRAY Inc.
why_relevant: Kyoto-based manufacturer of blood glucose monitoring devices since 1960. Kyoto Laboratory is their R&D hub. ARKRAY developed Japan's first quantitative blood glucose monitoring system in 1973. Produces GLUCOCARD meters and smartphone-linked glucose management apps
suggested_ask: Ask about data export format compatibility with Sugar-Sugar, and whether they would circulate an ethics-approved study invitation through their HCP or patient channels. Kyoto headquarters means a meeting is possible during the Kansai leg
dwih_angle: Kyoto-based: a natural meeting during the DWIH Kansai programme. Japanese diabetes device company with 60+ years of glucose measurement history
notes: Headquarters: Kyoto Miyuki Bldg. 10F, 689 Takanna-cho, Nakagyo-ku, Kyoto 604-8153. Tel: +81-50-5830-1000. ARKRAY does BGM not CGM, but they are expanding into connected health and their HCP network in Japan is the value

name: Terumo Corporation
why_relevant: Tokyo-based medical device giant founded 1921. Was exclusive Dexcom CGM distributor in Japan until March 2024; now developing digital therapy apps for diabetes with MICIN. Their Diabetes division knows the Japanese CGM landscape intimately
suggested_ask: Terumo no longer distributes Dexcom, so they may be looking for differentiation. Their MICIN diabetes app collaboration suggests digital health interest. Ask about the digital therapy programme and whether Sugar-Sugar's human baseline data could inform their prediction features
dwih_angle: Tokyo-based, major medical device company with active digital diabetes projects
notes: The Dexcom distribution ended, but the institutional knowledge of the Japanese CGM user base remains. Paired with MICIN for digital therapy; that programme is the entry point

name: Light Touch Technology (LTT) Inc.
why_relevant: Osaka-based venture developing the world's first non-invasive blood glucose sensor using mid-infrared laser technology. Spun off from QST (National Institutes for Quantum Science and Technology). Tamron invested January 2026. Clinical trials beginning 2026 for medical device approval
suggested_ask: Same framing as the non-invasive manufacturers in cgm-manufacturers-catalogue: offer to benchmark their prototype sensor traces against standard enzymatic CGM traces inside Sugar-Sugar. Non-invasive devices have a strong commercial incentive to join independent benchmarking
dwih_angle: Osaka-based deep tech startup in medical sensing - the closest Japanese parallel to DiaMonTech in the existing CGM catalogue. Perfect DWIH deep-tech demo: a German academic study benchmarking a Japanese sensing venture
notes: Pre-commercial, so no patient export format yet. The value is the deep-tech partnership narrative for DWIH and the future benchmarking once they have clinical data. Listed on Osaka's startup ecosystem portal

name: CureApp Inc.
why_relevant: Tokyo-based digital therapeutics startup. Developed prescription therapeutic apps for nicotine dependence (approved) and is building diabetes treatment support apps. Runs the DTx-BASE platform for pharmaceutical partners
suggested_ask: Ask about their diabetes therapeutic app programme and whether human glucose prediction accuracy data would inform their behavioural intervention models
dwih_angle: Tokyo-based health-tech with a diabetes digital therapy programme - a natural conversation partner for a study that measures human glucose prediction
notes: CureApp's diabetes app uses patient input to guide lifestyle changes. The connection is that Sugar-Sugar measures how well people actually predict glucose, which is the cognitive foundation their behaviour-change app assumes

name: MICIN Inc.
why_relevant: Tokyo (Chiyoda) digital health startup. Joint diabetes treatment support system with Terumo using lifestyle data and PHR
suggested_ask: Lower priority than CureApp or Terumo directly. The MICIN-Terumo project may be the entry point for Terumo itself
dwih_angle: Tokyo digital health company, part of the Terumo diabetes digital therapy ecosystem
notes: CEO Seigo Hara. Approach only if the Terumo contact suggests routing through MICIN

name: Dexcom Japan (direct operations)
why_relevant: Dexcom moved to direct distribution in Japan from April 2024, ending the Terumo partnership. Japan is a priority market with expanding reimbursement. The developer portal (developer.dexcom.com) grants instant sandbox credentials
suggested_ask: Contact the Japan office directly during the DWIH trip. Ask about local research partnerships and whether they would promote an ethics-approved prediction study to their Japanese user base
dwih_angle: Dexcom is already in cgm-manufacturers-catalogue globally. The Japan office is a separate contact point, reachable in person during the Launchpad
notes: The global Dexcom row in cgm-manufacturers-catalogue covers the developer and clinical research channels. This row is specifically for the Japan local office and in-person meeting during DWIH

name: Abbott Japan (FreeStyle Libre)
why_relevant: Abbott launched FreeStyle Libre 2 in Japan in March 2024 with NHI reimbursement for all insulin users (expanded April 2022). Largest CGM installed base in Japan
suggested_ask: Same channel as the global Abbott IIS process, but the Japan office may facilitate a local introduction. Libre is the format Sugar-Sugar already reads
dwih_angle: In-person meeting during DWIH to discuss the Japanese Libre user base as a recruitment channel
notes: The global Abbott row already covers the IIS submission process. This is the Japan-local angle. Dr Yoshihito Atsumi at Eiju General Hospital is a named Libre advocate - a possible clinical introduction

name: 糖尿病ネットワーク (Diabetes Network / dm-net.co.jp)
why_relevant: Japan's longest-running diabetes information portal, online since 1996. Run by Soshinsha Co. Ltd. Publishes news, patient resources, event listings, and the 1型ライフ (Type 1 Life) section. Active on X (@dmnet_jp), Facebook (DiabetesNetwork.JP) and YouTube
suggested_ask: Pitch a news item or event listing: an ethics-approved international study where Japanese adults can play a glucose prediction game. The 1型ライフ section is the direct fit
dwih_angle: The single most important Japanese-language diabetes media outlet found. Their event calendar already lists YOKOHAMA VOX and similar patient events
notes: Produced by Soshinsha Co. Ltd. No direct email found in search - use the contact form on dm-net.co.jp. Also runs 糖尿病リソースガイド (dm-rg.net) for healthcare professionals

name: 糖尿病リソースガイド (Diabetes Resource Guide / dm-rg.net)
why_relevant: HCP-facing diabetes news and resource site, sibling to dm-net.co.jp. Covers AI and digital health research in diabetes
suggested_ask: Pitch through the professional angle: an ethics-approved study establishing the first human baseline for CGM prediction accuracy
dwih_angle: The professional audience complements the patient audience of dm-net.co.jp. Same publisher, one pitch covers both
notes: Same publisher (Soshinsha) as dm-net.co.jp. Contact through the same channel

name: YOKOHAMA VOX (1型糖尿病セミナー)
why_relevant: Regular seminar series for type 1 diabetes patients in Yokohama. Group discussions cover CGM, Libre, pump therapy, daily management. The 39th meeting is upcoming in 2026
suggested_ask: Ask to present Sugar-Sugar at a future YOKOHAMA VOX session, or to have the study shared in their community channels. The CGM discussion group is the direct audience
dwih_angle: A patient community that already discusses CGM data and prediction in Japanese - the closest thing to a Sugar-Sugar focus group found in Japan
notes: Operations office: yokohama_vox@yahoo.co.jp. Events are listed on dm-net.co.jp. The CGM/Libre discussion group is specifically relevant

name: 本間太希 (Honma Taiki) - 1型糖尿病ランナー
why_relevant: 1型糖尿病 runner who was diagnosed at age 25. Cycling across Japan to raise diabetes awareness. Featured on TBS NEWS DIG as a diabetes influencer. Active on X/Twitter and YouTube
suggested_ask: Play-and-share ask: the exercise framing is the strongest hook - deciding whether to eat before a cycling day IS the next-hour prediction problem. Ask him to play a round and share his accuracy
dwih_angle: The most visible Japanese T1D lifestyle creator found. Exercise + T1D + Japanese language is the exact intersection the study needs for Japanese recruitment
notes: Verify current follower counts before contact. The exercise angle is the same one rated highest in the existing media-catalogue for English-language creators

name: 星南 (Sena) - model/talent with T1D
why_relevant: Model and talent who was diagnosed with T1D at age 18. Uses her platform to raise awareness and fight stigma against diabetes. Broader influencer reach beyond diabetes-specific audience
suggested_ask: Referral ask: her audience is general lifestyle, not diabetes-specific, so ask her to point adult followers at the study rather than a detailed CGM walkthrough
dwih_angle: Reaches a non-diabetes audience in Japanese, which is the non-diabetic arm of the study's recruitment
notes: Less directly on-topic than Honma Taiki but reaches people who would not otherwise encounter a glucose study

name: 糖尿病チャンネル (Diabetes Channel)
why_relevant: YouTube channel run by diabetes specialists providing evidence-based medical information about diabetes in Japanese. Professional clinical voice
suggested_ask: Pitch a feature or mention: an ethics-approved study establishing a human baseline for glucose prediction. The evidence-based framing suits their editorial standards
dwih_angle: Professional diabetes education channel in Japanese - the clinical credibility route into Japanese YouTube
notes: Verify subscriber count and posting frequency before contact. The channel name suggests an institutional or multi-physician operation rather than a solo creator

name: 糖と暮らし つじこ (Sugar Days / Tsujiko)
why_relevant: Japanese patient blogger on note.com writing about daily life with Libre 2, including real measurement errors and daily management challenges. Authentic first-person CGM experience writing
suggested_ask: Play-and-share ask: someone who writes about interpreting Libre curves is the ideal person to try predicting one. The game IS what they do every day, formalised
dwih_angle: Patient voice with direct Libre/CGM experience writing in Japanese
notes: Small audience but high authenticity. The note.com platform is where Japanese patient bloggers tend to publish (similar to Medium)

name: Renascience Inc. (レナサイエンス)
why_relevant: Tohoku University drug discovery venture focused on longevity research. CEO Keisuke Furuta. Opened TREx-Longevity Lab at Tohoku University in partnership with Northwestern University's Potocsnak Longevity Institute. Researching PAI-1 inhibitor RS5614 for aging-related conditions
suggested_ask: Research partnership: propose Sugar-Sugar as a quick functional phenotyping tool for their longevity cohorts - glucose prediction accuracy as a cognitive-metabolic marker
dwih_angle: Longevity biotech with academic roots - connects Anton's aging research background to the Japanese longevity ecosystem. Tohoku University is a potential institutional partner
notes: Located in Sendai (Miyagi Prefecture), not on the DWIH route, but reachable by Shinkansen from Tokyo. The longevity angle is enhancement.bio context, not direct Sugar-Sugar promotion

name: Japan Longevity Consortium
why_relevant: Multidisciplinary alliance of scientists, clinicians, wellness innovators. Ran the 1st World Longevity Summit in Kyotango. Affiliates include Kyoto Prefectural University of Medicine, University of Osaka, Altos Labs, Mitsubishi Research Institute
suggested_ask: Ask about presenting Sugar-Sugar at the next summit or consortium meeting. Frame glucose prediction as a functional biomarker of metabolic aging
dwih_angle: Bridges the longevity research community with the DWIH Kansai programme. The consortium already convenes the kind of audience that would appreciate the study
notes: ops@vitalism.io is the contact for the Tokyo Longevity Summit organised by related parties. Confirm whether the consortium itself has a separate contact

name: PHC Holdings / Ascensia Diabetes Care
why_relevant: Tokyo-based healthcare conglomerate (formerly Panasonic Healthcare). Subsidiary Ascensia Diabetes Care makes Contour glucose meters and historically distributed Senseonics Eversense in certain markets
suggested_ask: Low priority for direct Sugar-Sugar ask. PHC's diabetes care division uses BGM not CGM. Worth knowing as part of the Japanese diabetes device landscape
dwih_angle: Tokyo headquarters, part of the DWIH industry landscape
notes: HQ: 2-38-5 Nishishimbashi, Minato-ku, Tokyo 105-8433. IR: julia.cottrill@phchd.com. Ascensia is transferring Eversense distribution back to Senseonics, so this channel is closing

name: Vitalism Foundation / Tokyo Longevity Summit
why_relevant: Organises the Tokyo Longevity Summit bringing together startups, policymakers, investors and scientists. Speakers include VitaDAO representatives, Japanese VCs (Kind Capital), and longevity researchers. ~250 attendees
suggested_ask: Ask to present or exhibit at the next Tokyo Longevity Summit. Sugar-Sugar as a citizen-science tool for measuring a human metabolic capability is a natural demo
dwih_angle: The longevity startup event in Tokyo - connects to the DWIH deep-tech innovation narrative
notes: Contact: ops@vitalism.io. Adam Gries (Vitalism Foundation founder) and Eriko Suzuki (Kind Capital) are named speakers. The event is at Dragon Gate Hall, Shibuya Parco

name: EFSD-JDS Reciprocal Travel Research Fellowship
why_relevant: Bilateral programme between the European Foundation for the Study of Diabetes and the Japan Diabetes Society supporting travel for diabetes research collaboration between Europe and Japan
suggested_ask: Apply or explore eligibility: a German PI visiting Japanese diabetes research groups to present a human-baseline study and discuss data collaboration is exactly the programme's purpose
dwih_angle: The single most structurally aligned funding mechanism found. It exists to put European diabetes researchers in Japanese labs and vice versa
notes: Check current application deadlines and eligibility at europeandiabetesfoundation.org. The fellowship covers travel, which could overlap with or extend the DWIH trip
